title: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
summary: A physics-informed neural network derived plate orientations for isotropic metamaterial lattices. Simulations and manufactured six-plate samples showed stiffness near the Hashin–Shtrikman upper bound in tested geometries and near-isotropic behavior; the result does not establish general optimality.
ai_technology: Physics-informed neural network solving plate-orientation equations
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: PINN-derived lattices were assessed with finite-element simulations and manufactured six-plate geometries. Reported measurements include relative stiffness near 90% of the Hashin–Shtrikman upper bound at relative density 0.4 and near-isotropy in tested geometries.
evidence.unknown: Claims are bounded to the reported layouts and material/fabrication setup; no general optimality beyond tested geometries is established.
evidence.ai_role: A PINN solved analytical isotropy equations to derive plate orientations for lattice geometries.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
